status_summary: On the FACE Act, the President pardoned 24 individuals in five clinic-access cases on 2025-01-23 (DOJ Office of the Pardon Attorney), and a DOJ memorandum of 2025-01-24 directed dismissal of three pending cases and limited new abortion-related FACE Act actions to extraordinary circumstances with Civil Rights Division approval, while DOJ has continued to bring FACE Act cases over protests at houses of worship (2025-09-29 and 2026-02-27). On settlements and decrees, Attorney General memoranda of 2025-02-05 reinstated the bar on improper third-party settlement payments and directed components to review consent decrees and settlement agreements, and on 2025-05-21 DOJ moved to dismiss its Louisville police suit and to quash a proposed Minneapolis decree. Federal courts terminated the New Orleans and Newark police consent decrees (DOJ releases of 2025-11-19 and 2025-11-21) and the Edna Mahan Correctional Facility decree on 2026-07-15, each on motions DOJ joined or supported, and on 2026-09-24 DOJ announced it was ending more than 50 school desegregation cases through case-by-case review. On 2026-04-14 DOJ released a report of its Weaponization Working Group on FACE Act enforcement under the prior administration, whose findings outside groups dispute (NPR). On 2026-09-30 the District of New Jersey dismissed without prejudice, with leave to amend, DOJ's West Orange synagogue FACE Act suit, a ruling on one house-of-worship case that leaves the charging policy and decree terminations unaffected.

timeline.event: The President grants full and unconditional pardons to 24 unique individuals in five cases involving clinic-access offenses (DOJ Office of the Pardon Attorney; the warrant lists case captions, not offenses, and contains no direction to dismiss pending cases); NPR reports 23 pardons and three dropped cases, and the DOJ charging policy limiting new abortion-related FACE Act actions is dated the next day (see 2025-01-24).
timeline.source: DOJ Office of the Pardon Attorney; NPR

timeline.event: A DOJ memorandum on FACE Act charging policy from the Office of the Associate Attorney General directs immediate dismissal with prejudice of three pending civil FACE Act cases, limits new abortion-related FACE Act prosecutions and civil actions to extraordinary circumstances or significant aggravating factors such as death, serious bodily harm or serious property damage, and requires authorization from the Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights for any new such action.

Attorney General Bondi issues memoranda including 'Reinstating the Prohibition on Improper Third-Party Settlements' (settlements should not direct payments to non-governmental organizations that were neither victims nor parties, except in limited circumstances; rescinds the May 2022 guidelines and a July 2023 environmental division memo; the Associate Attorney General reports within 30 days) and 'Eliminating Internal Discriminatory Practices' (components review consent decrees and settlement agreements, grants and contracts for race- or sex-based preferences and DEI criteria, and consult the Office of Legal Counsel before acting contrary to a court order or decree). Lawfare also describes a Weaponization Working Group whose review includes prosecutions of anti-abortion activists.

DOJ moves to dismiss its Louisville police suit (ending a proposed, unapproved consent decree) and to quash a proposed Minneapolis decree, and says it will drop six police investigations including Memphis and Phoenix.
DOJ files a civil FACE Act suit in the District of New Jersey over a November 2024 protest at a West Orange synagogue, seeking an injunction.
A federal court terminates the 2013 New Orleans Police Department consent decree on a joint motion by DOJ and the city.
A federal court terminates the 2016 Newark Police Department consent decree on the city's motion, which DOJ supported.

DOJ announces 30 additional defendants, bringing the total to 39, in a District of Minnesota case over a protest at a St. Paul church, charged with a FACE Act misdemeanor and a felony conspiracy count; defendants have pleaded not guilty and a magistrate judge earlier rejected some warrants.

DOJ releases the first report of its Weaponization Working Group, on FACE Act enforcement under the prior administration; the release restates the 2025 pardons, the dismissal with prejudice of three civil FACE Act cases and the directive limiting abortion-related FACE Act actions to extraordinary circumstances. NPR reports at least four prosecutors were fired and that outside groups dispute the report's findings.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of Justice; NPR (via Georgia Public Broadcasting)

timeline.event: The U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey terminates the 2021 consent decree over the Edna Mahan Correctional Facility on a joint motion of DOJ and the State of New Jersey (DOJ release of 2026-07-16 dates the order to the previous day).
timeline.source: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey

timeline.event: DOJ announces it is ending more than 50 school desegregation cases from the 1960s and 1970s through a case-by-case review, seeking dismissal once a district has achieved unitary status.

The U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey (Judge Katharine S. Hayden) grants all six motions to dismiss in United States v. Party for Socialism and Liberation New Jersey, et al. (Civil No. 25-cv-16049, Document 113), the West Orange synagogue FACE Act suit, dismissing the single FACE Act count without prejudice as to each moving defendant and allowing the government to file an amended complaint within 30 days of the accompanying order.
